passages.text: At that time Hannah prayed: “My heart rejoices in the LORD in whom my horn is exalted. My mouth speaks boldly against my enemies, for I rejoice in Your salvation.
passages.sermon:
Hannah was a woman who prayed to God.
Hannah spoke these words.
Hannah said her heart rejoiced in the LORD.
Hannah said the LORD lifted up her strength.
Hannah said her mouth spoke boldly against her enemies.
Hannah said she rejoiced in God's salvation.
passages.original: וַתִּתְפַּלֵּ֤ל חַנָּה֙ וַתֹּאמַ֔ר עָלַ֤ץ לִבִּי֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה רָ֥מָה קַרְנִ֖י בַּֽיהוָ֑ה רָ֤חַב פִּי֙ עַל־ א֣וֹיְבַ֔י כִּ֥י שָׂמַ֖חְתִּי בִּישׁוּעָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: There is no one holy like the LORD. Indeed, there is no one besides You! And there is no Rock like our God.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is holy.
No one else is holy like the LORD.
No one exists besides the LORD.
No one is a rock like our God.
God is strong and unchanging.
God alone is our foundation.
passages.original: אֵין־ קָד֥וֹשׁ כַּיהוָ֖ה כִּ֣י אֵ֣ין בִּלְתֶּ֑ךָ וְאֵ֥ין צ֖וּר כֵּאלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Do not boast so proudly, or let arrogance come from your mouth, for the LORD is a God who knows, and by Him actions are weighed.
passages.sermon:
Hannah prayed to the LORD.
Hannah warned the people.
Do not speak with pride.
Do not let arrogance come from your mouth.
The LORD is a God who knows everything.
The LORD weighs every action.
passages.original: אַל־ תַּרְבּ֤וּ תְדַבְּרוּ֙ גְּבֹהָ֣ה גְבֹהָ֔ה יֵצֵ֥א עָתָ֖ק מִפִּיכֶ֑ם כִּ֣י אֵ֤ל דֵּעוֹת֙ יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹא נִתְכְּנ֖וּ עֲלִלֽוֹת׃

passages.text: The bows of the mighty are broken, but the feeble are equipped with strength.
passages.sermon:
God acts with power and justice.
God breaks the weapons of strong warriors.
Mighty people lose their strength.
Weak people receive strength from God.
God gives power to those who are feeble.
passages.original: קֶ֥שֶׁת גִּבֹּרִ֖ים חַתִּ֑ים וְנִכְשָׁלִ֖ים אָ֥זְרוּ חָֽיִל׃

passages.text: The well-fed hire themselves out for food, but the starving hunger no more. The barren woman gives birth to seven, but she who has many sons pines away.
passages.sermon:
God knows all things.
God weighs every action.
God changes people’s situations.
People who once had plenty of food now work for bread.
People who were hungry are hungry no longer.
A woman who could not have children now has seven children.
A woman with many children is sad and weak.
passages.original: שְׂבֵעִ֤ים בַּלֶּ֙חֶם֙ נִשְׂכָּ֔רוּ וּרְעֵבִ֖ים חָדֵ֑לּוּ עַד־ עֲקָרָה֙ יָלְדָ֣ה שִׁבְעָ֔ה וְרַבַּ֥ת בָּנִ֖ים אֻמְלָֽלָה׃

passages.text: The LORD brings death and gives life; He brings down to Sheol and raises up.
passages.sermon:
The LORD acts with power over life and death.
The LORD causes people to die.
The LORD gives life to people.
The LORD brings people down to Sheol, the place of the dead.
The LORD raises people up from Sheol.
passages.original: יְהוָ֖ה מֵמִ֣ית וּמְחַיֶּ֑ה מוֹרִ֥יד שְׁא֖וֹל וַיָּֽעַל׃

passages.text: The LORD sends poverty and wealth; He humbles and He exalts.
passages.sermon:
The LORD acts with power and authority.
The LORD gives poverty to people.
The LORD gives wealth to people.
The LORD humbles people.
The LORD exalts people.
passages.original: יְהוָ֖ה מוֹרִ֣ישׁ וּמַעֲשִׁ֑יר מַשְׁפִּ֖יל אַף־ מְרוֹמֵֽם׃

passages.text: He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the ash heap. He seats them among princes and bestows on them a throne of honor. For the foundations of the earth are the LORD’s, and upon them He has set the world.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the subject.
The LORD has power over all creation.
The LORD raises the poor from the dust.
The LORD lifts the needy from the ash heap.
The LORD seats the poor and needy among princes.
The LORD gives them a throne of honor.
The foundations of the earth belong to the LORD.
The LORD set the world upon these foundations.
passages.original: מֵקִ֨ים מֵעָפָ֜ר דָּ֗ל מֵֽאַשְׁפֹּת֙ יָרִ֣ים אֶבְי֔וֹן לְהוֹשִׁיב֙ עִם־ נְדִיבִ֔ים וְכִסֵּ֥א כָב֖וֹד יַנְחִלֵ֑ם כִּ֤י לַֽיהוָה֙ מְצֻ֣קֵי אֶ֔רֶץ וַיָּ֥שֶׁת עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם תֵּבֵֽל׃

passages.text: He guards the steps of His faithful ones, but the wicked perish in darkness; for by his own strength shall no man prevail.
passages.sermon:
The LORD protects His faithful people.
He watches over every step they take.
The LORD does not protect the wicked.
The wicked die in darkness.
No person can win by his own strength.
Only the LORD gives victory.
passages.original: רַגְלֵ֤י חֲסִידוֹ יִשְׁמֹ֔ר וּרְשָׁעִ֖ים בַּחֹ֣שֶׁךְ יִדָּ֑מּוּ כִּֽי־ לֹ֥א בְכֹ֖חַ יִגְבַּר־ אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: Those who oppose the LORD will be shattered. He will thunder from heaven against them. The LORD will judge the ends of the earth and will give power to His king. He will exalt the horn of His anointed.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
He has all power and authority.
Anyone who opposes the LORD will be broken.
The LORD will speak with thunder from heaven against His enemies.
The LORD will judge all people everywhere on earth.
The LORD will give strength to His chosen king.
The LORD will lift up and honor His anointed one.
passages.original: יְהוָ֞ה יֵחַ֣תּוּ מְרִיבוֹ עָלוֹ בַּשָּׁמַ֣יִם יַרְעֵ֔ם יְהוָ֖ה יָדִ֣ין אַפְסֵי־ אָ֑רֶץ וְיִתֶּן־ עֹ֣ז לְמַלְכּ֔וֹ וְיָרֵ֖ם קֶ֥רֶן מְשִׁיחֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: Then Elkanah went home to Ramah, but the boy began ministering to the LORD before Eli the priest.
passages.sermon:
Elkanah was a man from Ramah.
Elkanah went home to his house in Ramah.
The boy was Samuel.
Samuel began to serve the LORD.
Samuel served in the presence of Eli.
Eli was the priest.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ אֶלְקָנָ֛ה הָרָמָ֖תָה עַל־ בֵּית֑וֹ וְהַנַּ֗עַר הָיָ֤ה מְשָׁרֵת֙ אֶת־ יְהוָ֔ה אֶת־ פְּנֵ֖י עֵלִ֥י הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

passages.text: Now the sons of Eli were wicked men; they had no regard for the LORD or for the custom of the priests with the people. When any man offered a sacrifice, the servant of the priest would come with a three-pronged meat fork while the meat was boiling and plunge it into the pan or kettle or cauldron or cooking pot. And the priest would claim for himself whatever the meat fork brought up. This is how they treated all the Israelites who came to Shiloh.
passages.sermon:
The sons of Eli were wicked men.
They did not know the LORD.
They did not respect the custom of the priests with the people.
When any man offered a sacrifice, the servant of the priest would come.
He came while the meat was boiling.
He held a three-pronged meat fork in his hand.
He would plunge the fork into the pan, or the kettle, or the cauldron, or the cooking pot.
Whatever the fork brought up, the priest would take for himself.
They did this to all the Israelites who came to Shiloh.
passages.original: וּבְנֵ֥י עֵלִ֖י בְּנֵ֣י בְלִיָּ֑עַל לֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ אֶת־ יְהוָֽה׃ וּמִשְׁפַּ֥ט הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים אֶת־ הָעָ֑ם כָּל־ אִ֞ישׁ זֹבֵ֣חַ זֶ֗בַח וּבָ֨א נַ֤עַר הַכֹּהֵן֙ כְּבַשֵּׁ֣ל הַבָּשָׂ֔ר וְהַמַּזְלֵ֛ג שְׁלֹ֥שׁ־ הַשִּׁנַּ֖יִם בְּיָדֽוֹ׃ וְהִכָּ֨ה בַכִּיּ֜וֹר א֣וֹ בַדּ֗וּד א֤וֹ בַקַּלַּ֙חַת֙ א֣וֹ בַפָּר֔וּר כֹּ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר יַעֲלֶ֣ה הַמַּזְלֵ֔ג יִקַּ֥ח הַכֹּהֵ֖ן בּ֑וֹ כָּ֚כָה יַעֲשׂ֣וּ לְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַבָּאִ֥ים שָׁ֖ם בְּשִׁלֹֽה׃

passages.text: Even before the fat was burned, the servant of the priest would come and say to the man who was sacrificing, “Give the priest some meat to roast, because he will not accept boiled meat from you, but only raw.”
passages.sermon:
The sons of Eli were priests in Israel.
They were wicked men.
They did not know the LORD.
They did not respect the customs of the priests.
When a man brought a sacrifice, the servant of the priest would come.
This happened even before the fat was burned on the altar.
The servant would speak to the man who was offering the sacrifice.
He would say, “Give meat to the priest to roast.”
He would not accept boiled meat.
He wanted only raw meat.
passages.original: גַּם֮ בְּטֶרֶם֮ יַקְטִר֣וּן אֶת־ הַחֵלֶב֒ וּבָ֣א׀ נַ֣עַר הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְאָמַר֙ לָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֹּבֵ֔חַ תְּנָ֣ה בָשָׂ֔ר לִצְל֖וֹת לַכֹּהֵ֑ן וְלֹֽא־ יִקַּ֧ח מִמְּךָ֛ בָּשָׂ֥ר מְבֻשָּׁ֖ל כִּ֥י אִם־ חָֽי׃

passages.text: And if any man said to him, “The fat must be burned first; then you may take whatever you want,” the servant would reply, “No, you must give it to me right now. If you refuse, I will take it by force!”
passages.sermon:
A man would bring a sacrifice to the Lord.
The servant of the priest would ask for meat before the fat was burned.
Sometimes the man would answer the servant.
He would say, “First burn the fat today as required.
Then you may take whatever you desire.”
But the servant would not agree.
He would say, “No, you must give it to me now.
If you do not give it, I will take it by force.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו הָאִ֗ישׁ קַטֵּ֨ר יַקְטִיר֤וּן כַּיּוֹם֙ הַחֵ֔לֶב וְקַ֨ח־ לְךָ֔ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּאַוֶּ֖ה נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ וְאָמַ֥ר׀ לוֹ כִּ֚י עַתָּ֣ה תִתֵּ֔ן וְאִם־ לֹ֖א לָקַ֥חְתִּי בְחָזְקָֽה׃

passages.text: Thus the sin of these young men was severe in the sight of the LORD, for they were treating the LORD’s offering with contempt.
passages.sermon:
The young men were priests’ sons.
They sinned greatly.
The LORD saw their sin.
Their sin was very serious to the LORD.
These men showed contempt for the LORD’s offering.
They did not respect what belonged to God.
passages.original: וַתְּהִ֨י חַטַּ֧את הַנְּעָרִ֛ים גְּדוֹלָ֥ה מְאֹ֖ד אֶת־ פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֤י נִֽאֲצוּ֙ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים אֵ֖ת מִנְחַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Now Samuel was ministering before the LORD—a boy wearing a linen ephod.
passages.sermon: Samuel was a boy.\r\nSamuel served before the LORD.\r\nSamuel wore a linen ephod.
passages.original: וּשְׁמוּאֵ֕ל מְשָׁרֵ֖ת אֶת־ פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה נַ֕עַר חָג֖וּר אֵפ֥וֹד בָּֽד׃

passages.text: Each year his mother would make him a little robe and bring it to him when she went with her husband to offer the annual sacrifice.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a young boy.
His mother cared for him.
Each year, his mother made a small robe for him.
She brought the robe to Samuel every year.
She brought it when she went with her husband.
They went to offer the yearly sacrifice to the LORD.
passages.original: וּמְעִ֤יל קָטֹן֙ תַּעֲשֶׂה־ לּ֣וֹ אִמּ֔וֹ וְהַעַלְתָ֥ה ל֖וֹ מִיָּמִ֣ים׀ יָמִ֑ימָה בַּֽעֲלוֹתָהּ֙ אֶת־ אִישָׁ֔הּ לִזְבֹּ֖חַ אֶת־ זֶ֥בַח הַיָּמִֽים׃

passages.text: And Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, saying, “May the LORD give you children by this woman in place of the one she dedicated to the LORD.” Then they would go home.
passages.sermon:
Eli was the priest.
Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife.
Eli said, “May the LORD give you children by this woman.
May the LORD give you children to take the place of the child she dedicated to the LORD.”
Elkanah and his wife would then go home.
passages.original: וּבֵרַ֨ךְ עֵלִ֜י אֶת־ אֶלְקָנָ֣ה וְאֶת־ אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ וְאָמַר֙ יָשֵׂם֩ יְהוָ֨ה לְךָ֥ זֶ֙רַע֙ מִן־ הָאִשָּׁ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את תַּ֚חַת הַשְּׁאֵלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁאַ֖ל לַֽיהוָ֑ה וְהָלְכ֖וּ לִמְקֹמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So the LORD attended to Hannah, and she conceived and gave birth to three sons and two daughters. Meanwhile, the boy Samuel grew up in the presence of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD remembered Hannah.
Hannah became pregnant.
Hannah gave birth to three sons.
Hannah also gave birth to two daughters.
Samuel was Hannah’s first son.
Samuel was a boy.
Samuel grew up with the LORD.
Samuel lived in the presence of the LORD.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ פָקַ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ חַנָּ֔ה וַתַּ֛הַר וַתֵּ֥לֶד שְׁלֹשָֽׁה־ בָנִ֖ים וּשְׁתֵּ֣י בָנ֑וֹת וַיִּגְדַּ֛ל הַנַּ֥עַר שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל עִם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Now Eli was very old, and he heard about everything his sons were doing to all Israel and how they were sleeping with the women who served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
passages.sermon:
Eli was very old.
Eli heard about everything his sons did to all Israel.
Eli heard that his sons slept with the women.
These women served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
passages.original: וְעֵלִ֖י זָקֵ֣ן מְאֹ֑ד וְשָׁמַ֗ע אֵת֩ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲשׂ֤וּן בָּנָיו֙ לְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאֵ֤ת אֲשֶֽׁר־ יִשְׁכְּבוּן֙ אֶת־ הַנָּשִׁ֔ים הַצֹּ֣בְא֔וֹת פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃

passages.text: “Why are you doing these things?” Eli said to his sons. “I hear about your wicked deeds from all these people.
passages.sermon:
Eli was the high priest of Israel.
Eli had sons.
Eli spoke to his sons.
Eli said, “Why are you doing these things?”
Eli said, “I hear about your wicked deeds.”
Eli said, “All these people tell me about your actions.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ם לָ֥מָּה תַעֲשׂ֖וּן כַּדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֤י שֹׁמֵ֙עַ֙ אֶת־ דִּבְרֵיכֶ֣ם רָעִ֔ים מֵאֵ֖ת כָּל־ הָעָ֥ם אֵֽלֶּה׃

passages.text: No, my sons; it is not a good report I hear circulating among the LORD’s people.
passages.sermon:
Eli was very old.
Eli spoke to his sons.
He said, "No, my sons."
He said, "I hear a bad report about you."
He said, "This report is spreading among the LORD’s people."
He said, "This report is not good."
passages.original: אַ֖ל בָּנָ֑י כִּ֠י לֽוֹא־ טוֹבָ֤ה הַשְּׁמֻעָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָנֹכִ֣י שֹׁמֵ֔עַ מַעֲבִרִ֖ים עַם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: If a man sins against another man, God can intercede for him; but if a man sins against the LORD, who can intercede for him?” But they would not listen to their father, since the LORD intended to put them to death.
passages.sermon:
Eli was a priest and the father of two sons.
Eli spoke to his sons.
He said, “If a man sins against another man, God can intercede for him.
But if a man sins against the LORD, who can intercede for him?”
Eli’s sons did not listen to their father.
The LORD intended to put them to death.
passages.original: אִם־ יֶחֱטָ֨א אִ֤ישׁ לְאִישׁ֙ וּפִֽלְל֣וֹ אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְאִ֤ם לַֽיהוָה֙ יֶֽחֱטָא־ אִ֔ישׁ מִ֖י יִתְפַּלֶּל־ ל֑וֹ וְלֹ֤א יִשְׁמְעוּ֙ לְק֣וֹל אֲבִיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי־ חָפֵ֥ץ יְהוָ֖ה לַהֲמִיתָֽם׃

passages.text: And the boy Samuel continued to grow in stature and in favor with the LORD and with man.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a young boy.
Samuel grew taller.
Samuel became better in character.
The LORD was pleased with Samuel.
People also liked Samuel.
passages.original: וְהַנַּ֣עַר שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל הֹלֵ֥ךְ וְגָדֵ֖ל וָט֑וֹב גַּ֚ם עִם־ יְהוָ֔ה וְגַ֖ם עִם־ אֲנָשִֽׁים׃ס

passages.text: Then a man of God came to Eli and told him, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Did I not clearly reveal Myself to your father’s house when they were in Egypt under Pharaoh’s house?
passages.sermon:
A man of God came to Eli.
Eli was the high priest of Israel.
The man of God spoke to Eli.
He said, “This is what the LORD says.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD said, ‘I clearly revealed Myself to your father’s house.
I did this when your ancestors were in Egypt.
They were under Pharaoh’s house at that time.’”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א אִישׁ־ אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־ עֵלִ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הֲנִגְלֹ֤ה נִגְלֵ֙יתִי֙ אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔יךָ בִּֽהְיוֹתָ֥ם בְּמִצְרַ֖יִם לְבֵ֥ית פַּרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: And out of all the tribes of Israel I selected your father to be My priest, to offer sacrifices on My altar, to burn incense, and to wear an ephod in My presence. I also gave to the house of your father all the offerings of the Israelites made by fire.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Eli through a man of God.
God chose Eli’s father from all the tribes of Israel.
God appointed Eli’s father to be His priest.
God commanded Eli’s father to offer sacrifices on His altar.
God told Eli’s father to burn incense before Him.
God instructed Eli’s father to wear an ephod in God’s presence.
God gave Eli’s father’s house all the offerings made by fire from the Israelites.
passages.original: וּבָחֹ֣ר אֹ֠תוֹ מִכָּל־ שִׁבְטֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל לִי֙ לְכֹהֵ֔ן לַעֲל֣וֹת עַֽל־ מִזְבְּחִ֗י לְהַקְטִ֥יר קְטֹ֛רֶת לָשֵׂ֥את אֵפ֖וֹד לְפָנָ֑י וָֽאֶתְּנָה֙ לְבֵ֣ית אָבִ֔יךָ אֶת־ כָּל־ אִשֵּׁ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Why then do you kick at My sacrifice and offering that I have prescribed for My dwelling place? You have honored your sons more than Me by fattening yourselves with the best of all the offerings of My people Israel.’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Eli through a man of God.
God had chosen Eli’s family to serve as priests.
God had given them the right to offer sacrifices and receive offerings from Israel.
God said, “Why do you treat My sacrifice and My offering with contempt?”
I commanded these offerings for My dwelling place.
You have honored your sons more than you have honored Me.
You have allowed yourselves and your sons to become fat.
You have taken the best parts from all the offerings of My people Israel.
passages.original: לָ֣מָּה תִבְעֲט֗וּ בְּזִבְחִי֙ וּבְמִנְחָתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֖יתִי מָע֑וֹן וַתְּכַבֵּ֤ד אֶת־ בָּנֶ֙יךָ֙ מִמֶּ֔נִּי לְהַבְרִֽיאֲכֶ֗ם מֵרֵאשִׁ֛ית כָּל־ מִנְחַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְעַמִּֽי׃

passages.text: Therefore, the LORD, the God of Israel, declares: ‘I did indeed say that your house and the house of your father would walk before Me forever. But now the LORD declares: Far be it from Me! For I will honor those who honor Me, but those who despise Me will be disdained.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD said, “I promised that your house would serve Me forever.
I also promised that your father’s house would serve Me forever.
But now the LORD says, ‘I will not do this.
I will honor those who honor Me.
I will treat with contempt those who despise Me.’”
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן נְאֻם־ יְהוָה֮ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ אָמ֣וֹר אָמַ֔רְתִּי בֵּֽיתְךָ֙ וּבֵ֣ית אָבִ֔יךָ יִתְהַלְּכ֥וּ לְפָנַ֖י עַד־ עוֹלָ֑ם וְעַתָּ֤ה נְאֻם־ יְהוָה֙ חָלִ֣ילָה לִּ֔י כִּֽי־ מְכַבְּדַ֥י אֲכַבֵּ֖ד וּבֹזַ֥י יֵקָֽלּוּ׃

passages.text: Behold, the days are coming when I will cut off your strength and the strength of your father’s house, so that no older man will be left in your house.
passages.sermon:
God is speaking to Eli, the priest.
God says, “Days are coming.”
God will act in those days.
God will cut off your strength, Eli.
God will also cut off the strength of your father’s house.
No old man will remain in your house, Eli.
No one in your family will grow old.
passages.original: הִנֵּה֙ יָמִ֣ים בָּאִ֔ים וְגָֽדַעְתִּי֙ אֶת־ זְרֹ֣עֲךָ֔ וְאֶת־ זְרֹ֖עַ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑יךָ מִֽהְי֥וֹת זָקֵ֖ן בְּבֵיתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: You will see distress in My dwelling place. Despite all that is good in Israel, no one in your house will ever again reach old age.
passages.sermon:
God is speaking to Eli and his family.
God says, “You will see trouble in My house.
You will see this trouble even when I do good things for Israel.
No one in your family will ever grow old again.
This will last for all your days.”
passages.original: וְהִבַּטְתָּ֙ צַ֣ר מָע֔וֹן בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ יֵיטִ֖יב אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹֽא־ יִהְיֶ֥ה זָקֵ֛ן בְּבֵיתְךָ֖ כָּל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃

passages.text: And every one of you that I do not cut off from My altar, your eyes will fail and your heart will grieve. All your descendants will die by the sword of men.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Eli, the priest.
God said, “I will punish your family.
Some of your descendants will remain near My altar.
I will not remove every one of them.
But those who remain will suffer.
Your eyes will grow weak from sorrow.
Your heart will be full of grief.
Most of your family will die by violence.
Your descendants will be killed by men.
passages.original: וְאִ֗ישׁ לֹֽא־ אַכְרִ֤ית לְךָ֙ מֵעִ֣ם מִזְבְּחִ֔י לְכַלּ֥וֹת אֶת־ עֵינֶ֖יךָ וְלַאֲדִ֣יב אֶת־ נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ וְכָל־ מַרְבִּ֥ית בֵּיתְךָ֖ יָמ֥וּתוּ אֲנָשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: And this sign shall come to you concerning your two sons Hophni and Phinehas: They will both die on the same day.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Eli.
Eli had two sons.
Their names were Hophni and Phinehas.
God gave Eli a sign.
Both Hophni and Phinehas will die.
They will die on the same day.
passages.original: וְזֶה־ לְּךָ֣ הָא֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָבֹא֙ אֶל־ שְׁנֵ֣י בָנֶ֔יךָ אֶל־ חָפְנִ֖י וּפִֽינְחָ֑ס בְּי֥וֹם אֶחָ֖ד יָמ֥וּתוּ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then I will raise up for Myself a faithful priest. He will do whatever is in My heart and mind. And I will build for him an enduring house, and he will walk before My anointed one for all time.
passages.sermon:
God spoke these words.
God promised to act.
God said, “I will raise up a faithful priest for Myself.”
This priest will do everything that is in My heart.
This priest will do everything that is in My mind.
I will build a lasting house for this priest.
This priest will serve before My anointed one forever.
passages.original: וַהֲקִימֹתִ֥י לִי֙ כֹּהֵ֣ן נֶאֱמָ֔ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר בִּלְבָבִ֥י וּבְנַפְשִׁ֖י יַעֲשֶׂ֑ה וּבָנִ֤יתִי לוֹ֙ בַּ֣יִת נֶאֱמָ֔ן וְהִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ לִפְנֵֽי־ מְשִׁיחִ֖י כָּל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃

passages.text: And everyone left in your house will come and bow down to him for a piece of silver or a morsel of bread, pleading, “Please appoint me to some priestly office so that I can eat a piece of bread.” ’ ”
passages.sermon:
Everyone who remains in your house will come to him.
They will bow down before him.
They will ask for a piece of silver.
They will ask for a loaf of bread.
They will say, “Please appoint me to a priestly position.
Let me eat a piece of bread.”
passages.original: וְהָיָ֗ה כָּל־ הַנּוֹתָר֙ בְּבֵ֣יתְךָ֔ יָבוֹא֙ לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֣ת ל֔וֹ לַאֲג֥וֹרַת כֶּ֖סֶף וְכִכַּר־ לָ֑חֶם וְאָמַ֗ר סְפָחֵ֥נִי נָ֛א אֶל־ אַחַ֥ת הַכְּהֻנּ֖וֹת לֶאֱכֹ֥ל פַּת־ לָֽחֶם׃ס
